facts.heading: Exhaustion noted by GP
facts.content: Daniel's general practitioner suggested he come because she observed he looks exhausted.
facts.evidence: She said I look exhausted and she's right, I am.

facts.heading: Burnout started in October
facts.content: Daniel has been completely burnt out since October.
facts.evidence: I've been completely burnt out since October.

facts.heading: Workload increased after client loss
facts.content: Daniel's team lost a big client, and he ended up doing three people's jobs.
facts.evidence: We lost a big client, half of the team got moved onto the rescue plan, so I ended up doing three people's jobs.

facts.heading: Works long hours daily
facts.content: Daniel starts work at 7 am and continues answering messages until 10 pm.
facts.evidence: I'm at my desk by 7 and I'm still answering messages at 10 that night.

facts.heading: Sleep is poor
facts.content: Daniel sleeps about 4 hours most nights.
facts.evidence: Most nights I sleep about 4 hours.

facts.heading: Wakes at 3 am with anxiety
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at 3 am and worries about shipping schedules and the client.
facts.evidence: I wake up at 3 in the morning and just can't fall back asleep.

facts.heading: Father diagnosed with Parkinson's
facts.content: Daniel's father was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.
facts.evidence: My father. He was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease in the autumn.

facts.heading: Drives father to hospital
facts.content: Daniel drives his father to the hospital in Leeds for neurology appointments every few weeks.
facts.evidence: I'm the one who drives him to the hospital in Leeds. Neurology appointments are every few weeks, it's about an hour each way.

facts.heading: Daniel carries caregiving alone
facts.content: Daniel is the one handling all the care for his father because his sister Hannah lives in Toronto.
facts.evidence: all the care for our father falls of me.

facts.heading: Feels guilty about being tired
facts.content: Daniel feels selfish for being tired when his father is ill.
facts.evidence: He feels selfish to be tired when he's the one who's ill.

facts.heading: Girlfriend Claire is supportive
facts.content: Daniel's girlfriend, Claire, is patient and makes him tea.
facts.evidence: She's very patient. She makes me tea and doesn't push me to talk.

facts.heading: Cannot take weekend trips
facts.content: Daniel has been saying no to weekend trips because he anticipates receiving 200 emails upon return.
facts.evidence: I always said no. That's the thing I feel worst about actually.

facts.heading: Stopped running two months ago
facts.content: Daniel stopped running about two months ago because his legs feel like lead.
facts.evidence: I stopped about two months ago. My legs feel like lead.

facts.heading: Boss sends late emails
facts.content: Daniel's boss, Peterson, sends emails at 11 pm and expects answers before breakfast.
facts.evidence: he sends emails at 11 at night and expects an answer before breakfast.

facts.heading: Answers boss's late emails
facts.content: Daniel answers every email from his boss, even if he is not feeling well.
facts.evidence: I answer it. Every time. Even if I'm not bad.

facts.heading: Job insecurity due to restructuring
facts.content: Daniel is worried about being let go due to a restructuring happening this spring.
facts.evidence: There's a restructuring this spring and I'm afraid they'll let me go.

facts.heading: Financial responsibility
facts.content: Daniel has a mortgage.
facts.evidence: I have a mortgage.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms experienced
facts.content: Daniel experiences heart racing and shaking hands.
facts.evidence: My heart was going and my hands were shaking.

facts.heading: Past episodes of physical symptoms
facts.content: Daniel has experienced these symptoms a couple of times before.
facts.evidence: A couple of times.

facts.heading: Past symptom location
facts.content: One episode occurred on a train to Manchester.
facts.evidence: Once on a train to Manchester

facts.heading: Fear of losing control
facts.content: Daniel fears he is losing his mind or going to end up coping.
facts.evidence: That I'm losing it. That I'm going to end up, like, I don't know, coping.

facts.heading: Substance use for coping
facts.content: Daniel drinks about six cups of coffee daily.
facts.evidence: I want about six cups a day.

facts.heading: Evening wine consumption
facts.content: Daniel has started drinking wine in the evenings, consuming two to three glasses.
facts.evidence: And I've started having wine in the evenings to switch my head off. Two glasses, sometimes three.

facts.heading: Waking up early
facts.content: Daniel wakes up at three in the morning.
facts.evidence: I wake at three anyway.

facts.heading: Relief from sharing burdens
facts.content: Daniel felt a sense of relief after speaking about his burdens.
facts.evidence: A bit of relief actually.

facts.heading: Primary need is sleep
facts.content: Daniel believes if he could sleep, he could cope with other issues.
facts.evidence: If I could sleep, I could probably cope with the rest.

facts.heading: Family history of stoicism
facts.content: Daniel's grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire and never complained.
facts.evidence: My grandfather worked at the mines in Yorkshire. He never complained about anything.

facts.heading: Fear of disappointing grandfather
facts.content: Daniel fears his grandfather would think he was weak for being there.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking he would think I was weak for being here.

facts.heading: Plan to try phone restriction
facts.content: Daniel agreed to try switching off his phone for 20 minutes in the evening.
facts.evidence: Yeah, half past nine perhaps.

facts.heading: Plan to track sleep
facts.content: Daniel agreed to note how his night goes upon waking.
facts.evidence: I can do that. Right down when I wake up.

facts.heading: Current feeling state
facts.content: Daniel feels tired but lighter after the session.
facts.evidence: Tired, but lighter.
